construct: the compiled path on Windows (no compiled runtime; libc allocator fallback)
note: Section 10 makes the compiled artifact's block policy observable; on Windows the compiled runtime is not linked, so compile and link keep the libc path and `delete` releases host storage, but the counted-slab allocator is absent: there is no occupancy or fragmentation accounting, no block-reuse policy, no `memory.*` lowering, no runtime-wide routing (D1) and no task-end reclaim (D5). Closing the gap means linking the compiled runtime on Windows (the design's R8/T6) or splitting the allocator into a platform-neutral translation unit: size large, one runtime port or one allocator extraction, not a correction.
